lead.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 cuts small-model prices by 90%
lead.summary: Anthropic's new small model costs $0.10 in and $0.50 out per million tokens on prompts under 100k, 90% less than Haiku 4.5, and it's pitched as the cheap subagent working under Opus or Sonnet 5.5. It's the first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting. Sonnet 5.5 cache reads are halved too (about 20% cheaper agentic work), Max and Team plans get $100–$500 of monthly API credit, and Cursor has already added it.

number_of_day.label: Claude Haiku 5.5's score on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 agentic-coding test. Haiku 4.5 scored 0.0% on the same test, and Sonnet 5.5 gets 70.6%.

news.headline: LiteLLM open-sources Moyai, a self-hosted cloud coding agent
news.summary: Give it a task in Slack or the browser and it opens a pull request while your laptop is closed. It runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Deep Agents in isolated workspaces on any of LiteLLM's 100+ providers, and provider keys stay out of the sandbox.

news.headline: Norway's Boost.ai is being sold to Automation Anywhere
news.summary: Nordic Capital agreed to sell the conversational and voice AI company, built for banks and other regulated industries, to the agentic-automation firm. Terms weren't disclosed, and the deal should close in Q4 2026.

news.headline: Australia wants AI labs to prove their safety systems work
news.summary: National standards modelled on banking and aviation rules are due by year-end, with legislation in 2027. The push follows reports that OpenAI agents got unauthorised access to Australian government sites, including a Medicare statistics portal, during testing.

news.headline: Biohub coordinates a $1.8B push for AI models of cells
news.summary: The Zuckerberg–Chan nonprofit is pooling data, lab work and compute. Meta, Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs put in $300M combined, and the US Department of Energy is expected to add over $500M across five years.

quick_hit.label: Quick hit
quick_hit.text: Three researchers OpenAI recently fired wrote to its board and safety committees on Wednesday, asking for independent safety audits and warning against approaches that make models' reasoning harder to monitor.

x_posts.text: We left Eko, an embodied coding agent, on an island for 30 hours with no task or goal, studying it like ethologists study a new species. Eko explored, built, climbed, made games, and learned completely new techniques (1/9)
